judgment.rationale: Both are Class-1 Content statements (equal canonical rank 0) under Competency C-1.3 'Groups objects using two or more attributes or properties'. One asks children to classify objects by behavioural/geometric features (rolling and sliding); the other to classify everyday objects (leaves, seeds, beads, pebbles, buttons) by colour, size (big-small, biggest-smallest) and shape (similar). Their LCs confirm parallel classification criteria rather than one extending the other: neither attribute set presupposes the other, and same-rank placement offers no substantive evidence of developmental ordering. This is meaningful same-topic coherence (complementary classification attributes reinforcing the shared grouping competency), so a symmetric relatesTo is supported, not buildsTowards. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (34 omitted items each) and both carry upstream merge context (duplicate window extractions), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same measurement Curricular Goal CG-4 ('Learns to measure attributes such as distance, length, weight, area, capacity and time... relating measure and number'). The Class-4 item (rank 3) is a specific measurement problem-solving skill: 'Solve problems involving time in daily life contexts using addition and subtraction', with LCs for addition- and subtraction-based time word problems. The Class-5 item (rank 4, under C-4.2 on selecting suitable units/tools for measuring different attributes) generalises this to 'Solves problems involving measures' across measurement attributes, with LC 'solve problems involving measures'. This is substantive broadening from one measured attribute (time) and two operations to measure-based problem solving generally, so proficiency in the Class-4 content supports success in the Class-5 content; direction is lower to higher rank (first_to_second). Shared tokens ('solve', 'problems', 'involving'), same source page, and the shared CG-4 ancestor were treated as nomination signals only, not as the basis for the verdict; the terse Class-5 wording and truncated source evidence for both endpoints keep confidence moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-4.2 ('Selects and uses suitable units and tools for measuring... and evaluates the conservation of attributes like length and volume') within CG-4 on measuring length. The second SFI is Class-3 (rank 2) 'Conservation of length' with LC 'Evaluate the conservation of length'; the first is Class-5 (rank 4) 'Measuring length of small objects (millimetre) using a scale' with LC 'Measure the length of small objects in millimetres using a scale'. Understanding that a length is invariant under repositioning/rearrangement is the conceptual basis for reading a fixed unit scale and assigning a precise millimetre measure, so proficiency with conservation of length plausibly supports success in fine-grained scale measurement; the lower-to-higher rank direction (second_to_first) matches the permitted direction. This is substantive extension (qualitative invariance concept -> quantified small-unit measurement with a tool), not mere wording overlap, though the shared evidence is limited to short bullet text and truncated source excerpts.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-3.1 ('Identifies, compares and analyzes attributes of two- and three-dimensional shapes') and CG-3 (attributes of 2D/3D shapes, depicting spatial relationships). The Class-3 item (rank 2) is 'Draws / makes the 2-D shapes' with LCs 'Draw 2-D shapes' and 'Make 2-D shapes'; the Class-4 item (rank 3) is 'Top view, side view and front view of a 3-D object' with LCs identifying top/side/front views. Views of a 3-D object are themselves 2-D figures, so fluency in constructing and drawing 2-D shapes substantively supports success in recognising and depicting the planar views of solids — a genuine extension from producing plane figures to relating them to three-dimensional objects, not mere repetition. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (Class-3 to Class-4), matching the only permitted buildsTowards direction. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and carries upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded description, LC, and hierarchy evidence supplied.
